items.title: Gene Bertoncini interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: I fell in love with the music of — aside from jazz players — the music of Julian Bream, a great English guitarist

ctx.x: Do you think that had any effect on — that interest — in the way you play?

Yeah. Yeah I do. I like to plan stuff. I like to — when I play a piece of music I usually arrange it and I usually think of a concept for it, and have an area where there’s improvisation. I like to think of the guitar as my little orchestra, or a big band. And I do arrangements for my big band. And I play them and I work out fairly complicated things. I was fortunate in that I fell in love with the music of — aside from jazz players — the music of Julian Bream, a great English guitarist and I heard his…
That’s right. It gets a little unwieldy.
